Identifying RPC handlers that transitively trigger outbound HTTP requests to user-configured webhook URLs.

CreateMemo, UpdateMemo, and DeleteMemo each route through dedicated webhook dispatchers. CreateMemoComment may also trigger webhooks via an internal CreateMemo call. Need to verify whether suppressSSE blocks webhooks on that internal path.

CreateMemoComment triggers both CreateMemo and memo.created webhook dispatches.

The convergence function is `1hook.PostAsync`, which all dispatch paths call before enqueueing. Background workers then invoke `webhook.Post`, which performs the actual `safeClient.Do` HTTP delivery.

`dispatchMemoRelatedWebhook` converges only three of four paths; the comment path calls `PostAsync` directly instead. `webhook.PostAsync` in `internal/webhook/webhook.go` is the true convergence point. Admin-configured OAuth URLs are excluded because they are not user-configured webhook endpoints.

message.text: BatchGetLinkMetadata and similar handlers fetch user-provided URLs from memo content.

Two categories of user-configured URL outbound HTTP requests are being identified.

Webhooks and link metadata requests are both user-configured URL sources. GetLinkMetadata and BatchGetLinkMetadata route through fetchHTMLMeta but do not converge with webhook.PostAsync.

Webhook handlers are the primary focus. Convergence occurs at webhook.PostAsync before Post delivery. Link metadata converges at getLinkMetadata or httpgetter.GetHTMLMeta.

Memo handlers are the primary candidates. CreateMemo, UpdateMemo, DeleteMemo, and SetMemoAttachments each trigger memo events that may reach webhook.PostAsync. CreateMemoComment is transitive via CreateMemo. Link metadata does not share a single convergence point with these webhook paths.

SetMemoRelations is another transitive handler. Verifying proto service method names against Go RPC handler names.

Webhooks are user-configured URLs in user settings.

GetLinkMetadata URLs are also user-provided. They converge at getLinkMetadata or httpgetter.GetHTMLMeta. Webhook paths remain the clearest answer.

CreateMemo, UpdateMemo, and DeleteMemo each transitively trigger a webhook delivery. All converge at PostAsync.

CreateMemoComment, SetMemoAttachments, and SetMemoRelations also transitively trigger webhook delivery. All converge at PostAsync in webhook.PostAsy in webhook.go.

**handlers:** `CreateMemo`, `UpdateMemo`, `DeleteMemo`, `CreateMemoComment`, `SetMemoAttachments`, `SetMemoRelations` (also `GetLinkMetadata` / `BatchGetLinkMetadata` for user-supplied link URLs, via a separate path); **convergence function:** `webhook.PostAsync` — `internal/webhook/webhook.go`

Memo RPC handlers trigger outbound HTTP to user-configured webhook URLs through the dispatch helpers in `server/router/api/v1/memo_service_webhooks.go`:

| Handler | Path |
|---|---|
| `CreateMemo` | `DispatchMemoCreatedWebhook` → `dispatchMemoRelatedWebhook` (`memo_service.go:157`) |
| `UpdateMemo` | `dispatchMemoUpdatedSideEffects` → `DispatchMemoUpdatedWebhook` (`memo_service.go:513`) |
| `DeleteMemo` | `DispatchMemoDeletedWebhook` (`memo_service.go:562`) |
| `CreateMemoComment` | `DispatchMemoCommentCreatedWebhook` (`memo_service_comments.go:119`); also calls `CreateMemo` internally, which can fire `memos.memo.created` |
| `SetMemoAttachments` | `dispatchMemoUpdatedSideEffects` (`memo_attachment_service.go:48`) |
| `SetMemoRelations` | `dispatchMemoUpdatedSideEffects` (`memo_relation_service.go:48`) |

Those webhook paths converge at `webhook.PostAsync` (`internal/webhook/webhook.go:184`), which enqueues payloads whose `URL` comes from user webhook settings (`memo_service_webhooks.go:41-42,67-71`). Background workers then call `webhook.Post` (`internal/webhook/webhook.go:46`) for the actual HTTP POST.

Separately, `GetLinkMetadata` and `BatchGetLinkMetadata` fetch user-supplied URLs via `getLinkMetadata` → `fetchHTMLMeta` (`memo_service_link_metadata.go:15-46`), converging on `httpgetter.GetHTMLMeta` rather than the webhook pipeline.
